claim.why_it_matters: 2.4 is a sibling of 2.1 ('###' on page 857); at '##' it is rendered at the level of clause 2, a wrong heading level.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 859 (folio A-29) prints '2.4 DEFINITIONS OF FUNCTIONS' as a bold run-in numbered subsection heading, styled the same as '2.3 TYPES OF FUNCTIONS' above it. The transcription has the heading text verbatim, but as '## 2.4 DEFINITIONS OF FUNCTIONS'. In the same Section A of the transcription, '## 2. GENERAL DESCRIPTION' and '### 2.1 FUNCTION DEFINITION AND RETURNED VALUE' (page 857) set the levels, so 2.4 at '##' sits beside clause 2 and not under it as a child. That puts the wrong section tree into the markdown. It is a real structural defect. The claim's kind 'missing-heading' is wrong: the heading is present with the correct text and only its level is wrong. (The '## 2.3 TYPES OF FUNCTIONS' heading on the same page has the same level error.)
verdict.corrected_description: Wrong heading level, not a missing heading: the transcription renders '2.4 DEFINITIONS OF FUNCTIONS' as '##', the level of '## 2. GENERAL DESCRIPTION'. It should be '###', the level of its sibling '### 2.1' on page 857. The text matches the PDF.
